data.title: Europe's Truck Makers Face Danger From China's Electric Edge — Market Talk
data.description: Europe's truck makers face an increasing threat from Chinese manufacturers focused on electric trucks, Metzler Capital Markets says in a note. Developments show China's head start, with nearly 40% of new truck registrations in the first 10 months in China consisting of vehicles with alternative powertrains, while in Europe the share of electric trucks was 5.5% in 1H, Metzler says. While China goes electric, Europeans have a more open strategy technologically that reduces short-term risks but carries the danger--as shown with cars--of falling behind in terms of scaling up electric trucks. In China, factors like state support and expanding infrastructure foster the trend, putting Europe's commercial vehicle industry under pressure to adjust strategically, Metzler says. (sarah.sloat@wsj.com)

data.title: Climate Focus: Thanksgiving disruptions as storm hits US East Coast
data.description:
By Sharon Kimathi

A powerful storm disrupted the Thanksgiving holiday along much ‌of the US East Coast, knocking out power to nearly 1 million customers at one point as wind gusts of up to 70 mph (112 kph) toppled trees and power lines.

Heavy rains flooded coastal areas, while utilities warned of an increased risk of falling trees ​and power outages.

Storms bringing heavy rain and winds up and down ​the Eastern Seaboard also delayed flights during one of the ‌busiest travel weeks of the year.

The 100th edition of the annual Macy's ​Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City was also postponed for two days until Saturday due to the storm, marking the first time the event has been rescheduled due to severe weather.

Rainfall rates could reach 1 inch (2.5 cm) per hour at ​times, with wind gusts exceeding 50 mph (80 kph), according to the National Weather ​Service.

The NWS issued a coastal flood warning for the San Francisco Bay Area through late Thursday afternoon, warning that flooding could reach 2.7 feet (0.8 meter) in some ​low-lying areas as near-record high tides swell the region's waterways.

Separately on Thursday, President Donald Trump said he had approved about $100 million in federal ⁠aid ​to Florida following severe storms and flooding there. He ​said the total included funding previously approved in connection with Hurricane Isaias.

Click here to watch a live weather map showing the storm moving across the US East Coast.

Climate Buzz

  • OPEC blames EU for COP31 collapse

In a blog post titled "What Really Happened at COP31?", OPEC Secretary General Haitham Al Ghais rejected claims that Saudi Arabia, Russia and other oil producers were responsible for the failure of talks in Antalya. The countries had opposed language on transitioning away from fossil fuels. Al Ghais also directed blame for the failure of the talks at the European Union and others, accusing the EU of hypocrisy, ​saying it called for a move away from hydrocarbons while simultaneously easing some of its own energy regulations.

  • European emissions proposal faces Middle East pushback at UN aviation agency

Middle East countries pushed back against new efforts to curb airline emissions at a global aviation meeting this week, after proposed changes to the European Union's Emissions Trading System. Saudi Arabia urged countries to back the aviation sector's existing global carbon scheme, CORSIA, as the sole mechanism for cutting emissions from international flights.

  • Thailand moves to pin down source of Myanmar mine river pollution

Thailand plans to present Myanmar with evidence by January that rare earth mining across the border is polluting downstream rivers, Deputy Prime Minister Yodchanan Wongsawat told Reuters. Mining has surged in militia-controlled areas of Myanmar in recent years, driven in part by demand from China's rare earth industry, but lax environmental controls have also put downstream communities at risk.

  • The search for Vietnam's stolen pets at wet markets and slaughterhouses

Vietnamese police report detaining scores of suspected pet thieves this year, accused of stealing thousands of cats and dogs to sell for slaughter as their meat is legal in Vietnam. The criminals are operating at the nexus of a cultural shift in the country of 100 million people, drawn largely along generational lines. Click here for the insightful story and video.

  • Italy weighs biggest hunting expansion in years, alarming wildlife groups

Italian lawmakers are weighing up the biggest overhaul of hunting legislation since 1992 with plans that would recast hunters as wildlife managers and allow more animals to be hunted. Environmentalists warn the measures could lead to widespread culling and threaten protected species. It follows lobbying by hunting and farming groups ahead of a general election due next year.

What to Watch​

About 60% of Japan’s data centers are in and around the densely populated Tokyo metropolitan area, home to about 37 million people, and growing opposition from residents has prompted a review ​of an industry the government is counting on to drive economic growth. Click here for the full video and story following residents fighting against these data centers.

Climate Commentary

  • Are COPs a waste of time and carbon? Or should the question be: what if COPs didn’t exist at all? Click here to find out the answer in a piece for Ethical Corp Magazine by Marco Lambertini, the convenor of Nature Positive Initiative, a global biodiversity coalition.

  • Electrification, a push for clean power and phasing out existing fossil fuels, could take more than 0.5 degrees Celsius off our current trajectory of 2.64 degrees of warming, writes Ethical Corp Magazine contributor Angeli Mehta. But how we make that switch matters. Click here to find out more.

Climate Lens

The ‌scale of ⁠the current El Nino has changed the debate around ensuring countries' climate resilience, with discussions increasingly focused on immediate concerns such as food security. Click here to find out more about how the weather phenomenon will affect farmers.

Number of the Week

65%

That's the percentage of Germany's electricity generated by wind over the first three weeks of the month, up from just 6%, as wind output surged from less than 100 gigawatt hours to more than 1,100 GWh. What does this mean for fossil fuels? Click here to find out more in a piece by Reuters global energy transition columnist Gavin Maguire.

data.title: S&P outlook downgrade could be on the cards for France
data.description:
Key points:
  • STOXX up 1%, as stock markets bounce globally
  • Miners, tech lead gains
  • S&P futures up 1.5%

S&P OUTLOOK DOWNGRADE COULD BE ON THE CARDS FOR FRANCE

S&P review France's rating later on Friday, and Citi think there is a chance they could lower their outlook which they say would be "another brick in the wall of worry" for French bonds.

S&P rates France at A+, on par with Fitch but below Moody’s (Aa3), and it is the only major rating agency that has France still on a stable outlook.

However, Citi point out that at their June review, S&P forecast 0.8% and 1.1.% real GDP growth in 2026 and 2027, and 5.1% and 4.7% government deficit.

And they say "it seems very likely that French growth will fall short of S&P’s expectations," flagging growth around the flatline and noting that "October PMIs for France point to further weakness."

France's economy contracted more than initially thought in the third quarter as the country technically dipped into recession, final data from the national statistics office showed on Friday.

S&P said in the June analysis it “could lower our ratings on France if its budgetary position deteriorates beyond our forecast or economic growth prospects worsen significantly".

They say "as both these conditions appear to have been met, there is a possibility that S&P will follow Fitch’s lead and lower France’s Outlook. "

They don't think that will materially move OATs that already trade at a wider spread to Germany's than other major Euro zone government bonds.

But it wouldn't help either.

data.title: Benton Acquires Additional Strategic Land Within Its Dominion Gold-Base Metal Project, Newfoundland
data.description:
Thunder Bay, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Benton Resources Inc. ("Benton" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that the Company has acquired a strategic parcel of land consisting of 18 claim units in one mineral licence, contiguous to and within its Dominion land package. The Company has signed a purchase agreement with three arm's-length individuals (the "Vendors") who currently hold the licence. The land parcel sits in the south-central part of Benton's Dominion project and approximately 1.5km SW of Canterra Minerals Corporation's Daniel's Pond VMS deposit (see Figure 1).

Subject to TSX Venture Exchange approval, the Company will make a one-time payment of $12,000 and issue 120,000 shares, which will be allocated equally among the Vendors. The Vendors will retain a 2.0% NSR subject to the right of the Company to purchase back 1.0% for $1.0 million dollars. There were no finders' fees paid in connection with this acquisition.

Figure 1: Dominion Property Trenching Area Map and Location of Newly Acquired Licence

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

The Company began assembling the Dominion project in November 2023, after a large parcel of land became available for staking and has since accumulated a very large and prospective land position.

A news release on September 10th, 2026, announced the first channel sample results from the new Rickirb gold zone delivering highlights of 11.2 m of 1.80 g/t Au incl. 3.0 m of 6.36 g/t Au and 1.0 m of 10.58 g/t Au, 2.0 m of 8.00 g/t Au, incl. 0.5 m of 30.53 g/t Au and 3.7 m of 4.20 g/t Au, incl. 0.9 m of 15.29 g/t Au. The Rickirb gold zone remains completely open in all directions. In addition, a news release dated October 8th, 2026, announced a second discovery at the Quinlan Zone including highlights of 6.59 g/t Au over 6.0 m, incl 37.87 g/t Au over 1.0 m and 3.84 g/t Au over 5.0 m incl. 18.28 g/t Au over 1.0 m.

QP

Stephen House (P.Geo.), Vice President of Exploration for Benton Resources Inc., the 'Qualified Person' under National Instrument 43-101, has approved the scientific and technical disclosure in this news release and prepared or supervised its preparation.

QA/QC Protocols

Core and rock samples, including standards, blanks and duplicates, are submitted to Eastern Analytical Ltd., Springdale, Newfoundland for preparation and analysis. All samples were acquired by saw-cut (channels/drill core) with one-half submitted for assay and one-half retained for reference, or hand (rocks) and delivered, by Benton personnel, in sealed bags, to the Springdale lab, which is an accredited assay lab that conforms to the requirements of ISO/IEC 17025. Samples are analyzed by Au Fire assay @ 30 g + ICP-34 method that delivers a 34-element package utilizing a 200 mg subsample totally dissolved in four acids and analyzed by ICP-OES analytical technique. Overlimits are analyzed using the atomic absorption method, using a 0.200 g to 2.00 g of sample, digested with three acids. All reported assays are uncut. Eastern achieved ISO 17025 accreditation in February 2014 (for more details on the scope of accreditation visit the CALA website). Grab samples are selective in nature and may not represent the average mineralization of a bedrock exposure.

About Benton Resources Inc.

Benton Resources is a well-financed mineral exploration company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol BEX. Benton is currently planning a spinout to shareholders of its high-grade Great Burnt copper-gold project, has a diversified, highly prospective property portfolio and holds large equity positions in other mining companies that are advancing high-quality assets. Whenever possible, BEX retains net smelter return (NSR) royalties with potential long-term cash flow.

Benton is focused on advancing its Dominion Copper-Zinc-Gold project, Victoria West/South Gold Projects, Stoney Caldera Copper-Gold Project and its various Hydrogen-Helium projects on the west coast of Newfoundland.

data.title: BAE Systems secures five-nation landmark agreement worth $6B for new CV90 combat vehicles
data.description:
STOCKHOLM, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BAE Systems (LON: BA) has been awarded contracts worth a total of $6 billion in a joint procurement with Finland, Lithuania, Netherlands, Norway and Sweden for the delivery of more than 400 CV90 combat vehicles.

This landmark joint agreement for the CV9035 MkIV Nordic Edition is a world first; bringing five nations together under one deal and leading the way for the future of allied nation procurements.

Awarded under separate Purchase Order Agreements (POA) referring to the same framework agreement defining the vehicle configuration, the procurements will significantly strengthen the defences of the participating nations' armed forces and increase interoperability and readiness for the region.

"This procurement demonstrates the strength of the Nordic and allied cooperation, and it underscores the trust placed in the CV90 family – now expanded with Lithuania – as the backbone of modern, highly capable, mechanized forces," said Tommy Gustafsson-Rask, general manager at BAE Systems Hägglunds. "The CV9035 MkIV Nordic Edition combines combat-proven performance with the latest digital, protection and lethality upgrades, ensuring our customer nations can operate seamlessly together for decades to come. We are proud to support this long-term partnership and to contribute to security and industrial resilience across the region."

The extensive programme also includes related support systems, such as technical publications, training, spare parts, special tools and test equipment.

A distributed supplier network located in the participating nations will produce the vehicles and components; creating a transfer of technical knowledge and strengthening the security of supply of vital infantry fighting vehicles (IFV) in the region.

The common IFV configuration creates synergies beneficial to development, spare part lead times, integrated logistic support, sustainment and operations. The commonality also provides considerable benefits to existing users to improve operational readiness, such as reduced time and cost for training, easier crew transitions and simplified maintenance.

data.title: Indonesia central bank governor expects 2027 GDP growth of 5.2% to 6%
data.description:
Indonesia's central bank predicted 2027 GDP growth would reach 5.2% to 6.0%, slightly higher than this year's forecast of 4.9% to 5.7%, its governor told an annual bankers' dinner, unchanged from forecasts shared in September.

  • Destry Damayanti said economic resilience would continue in 2027

  • She expected loan growth at 9% to 13% in 2027, also higher than 2026's 8% to 12% range.

  • Monetary policy will be directed at maintaining financial market stability in 2027, Destry said

  • Rupiah stabilisation measures will be strengthened next year, she said

  • Bank Indonesia has raised rates by 125 basis points since May to support the falling rupiah currency

  • The rupiah has lost more than 9% against the US dollar so far this year

  • On Friday the currency strengthened 0.3%, but the previous day it had hit a record low of 18,395 per dollar

data.title: Coca-Cola continues its refranchising strategy with a deal in Africa
data.description:
Coca-Cola Company and Gutsche Family Investments have completed the sale of a 75% controlling interest in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa Pty. Ltd. to Coca-Cola HBC AG after receiving all necessary regulatory approvals in Africa.

Coca-Cola Beverages Africa is a Johannesburg-based company and the largest Coca-Cola bottler in Africa. It operates in 14 countries and handles about 40% of all Coca-Cola volume sold on the continent. It was formed by merging the Southern and East African bottling businesses of The Coca-Cola Company , SABMiller, and Gutsche Family Investments and began operating as its own company in July 2016. In October 2025, Coca-Cola and Gutsche Family Investments agreed to sell a 75% stake to Swiss-based Coca-Cola HBC for about $2.6B, valuing CCBA at $3.4B.

Of note, Coca-Cola and Coca-Cola HBC have a separate option agreement providing Coca-Cola HBC the opportunity to acquire the remaining 25% stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa held by Coca-Cola within a six-year period.

The completion of the transaction was noted to mark another significant milestone in Coca-Cola's ongoing strategy to refranchise company-owned and controlled bottling operations. "This transaction reflects the strength of the Coca-Cola system and our long-term commitment to building locally led, world-class bottling operations," stated Coca-Cola CEO Henrique Braun. "CCBA has established a strong foundation across Africa, and Coca-Cola HBC brings proven capabilities, deep market expertise, and a successful track record of investing for sustainable growth," he added.

data.title: Zoomlion Showcases Advanced Electric Equipment and Integrated Energy Solutions at bauma CHINA 2026
data.description:
SHANGHAI, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zoomlion Heavy Industry Science & Technology Co., Ltd. ("Zoomlion" or "the Company") unveiled a series of electric equipment innovations at bauma CHINA 2026, including the world's largest 300-ton distributed electric-drive crawler crane and the world's first 55-ton-class all-electric rubber-tired port crane. The Company is also showcasing electric equipment for concrete construction, transportation, and mining operations, with new-energy products making up half of the more than 60 products and systems on display.

How is Zoomlion advancing equipment electrification?

Zoomlion's new-energy equipment portfolio now covers its three core industrial segments of construction, agricultural, and mining machinery. The Company is developing multiple power and energy supply technologies, including battery-electric, grid-powered, hybrid, and hydrogen fuel solutions. This diversified approach means that Zoomlion can provide customers with equipment and solutions that are suited to specific applications, operating conditions, and power supply infrastructure.

How can electric cranes meet demanding lifting requirements?

Zoomlion's ZCC3000AEV 300-ton distributed electric-drive crawler crane features a 400 kWh battery pack that can support at least 24 hours of operation on a single charge. Its dual-connector DC fast-charging system delivers up to 240 kW of charging power that enables a full charge in two hours. The crane can also charge and operate simultaneously through its AC charging system, helping to minimize downtime during extended construction projects. Developed specifically for port operations, Zoomlion's 55-ton-class all-electric rubber-tired port crane features a multi-motor drive system and supports more than 24 hours of operation. The crane, compatible with various attachments, including those for pulp handling and electromagnetic lifting, addresses diverse cargo handling requirements while delivering zero exhaust emissions and low-noise operation.

Su Min, general manager of Zoomlion's Mobile Crane Division, said: "Demand for electrification across global markets encompasses carbon emissions reduction, noise reduction, environmental protection, road access, operating efficiency, and control precision. Our products are developed around these specific requirements in order to balance the broader societal benefits of greener equipment with actual operating performance."

How does electrification support concrete construction and transportation?

Zoomlion's world-first 73-meter all-electric concrete pump truck features independent drive systems for the chassis and pumping equipment that reduce overall energy consumption by over 46%. Its 352 kWh lithium iron phosphate battery provides a driving range that exceeds 200 kilometers, while a 120 kW plug-in system enables operation using a 380 V industrial power supply. For concrete transportation, Zoomlion is also showcasing an electric mixer truck that can gain 50 kilometers of driving range with just nine minutes of charging. These innovations offer customers greater flexibility through battery power, direct grid connection, and rapid charging by addressing both transportation and on-site operating requirements.

How can electric equipment and microgrids support mining operations?

Zoomlion's ZE4000GEL 400-ton-class cable-powered electric excavator, designed for demanding mining environments, features a 1,500 kW electric motor. Its automatic cable reel system enables continuous grid-powered operation while allowing the excavator to move freely within a 300-meter operating range. In addition to individual electric machines, Zoomlion is integrating power generation, distribution, consumption, energy storage, and charging infrastructure into mining microgrid solutions. These microgrid solutions are designed to coordinate power supply and equipment operations through the Company's smart mining platform.

Zoomlion will continue expanding the application of electric equipment and supporting energy solutions to address the diverse operating cycles, power supply conditions, and construction environments of its global customers.
